attempts.paper_title: Sub-microsecond optical measurements of cell membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields
attempts.entry_title: Membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields (Semenov et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Almost none of the paper's findings could be tested here, and none was shown to fail. The dandiset holds FluoVolt time courses of single 1-us pulses, not the paper's Di-8-ANEPPS and FluoVolt escalation sets, so the polarization pattern, the loss of pole charging at electroporating fields, and the Gd3+, calcium and two-pulse resealing results could not be tested. The one claim needing no recordings, the effect of membrane conductivity on charging, partly held: the 100-fold value matches, but a 10-fold rise gives 1.3% where the paper says about 2%.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Semenov et al. (2026) on dandiset 001515, which holds FluoVolt strobe-imaging time courses of CHO cells charged by single 1-us pulses at one amplitude per cell. None of the paper's experiments (sets of 40 baseline and 60 pulse images at 900 ns with field escalation, Di-8-ANEPPS, 0.3-us pulses, Gd3+, two-pulse and Ca2+ recordings) is in it, so 33 of 34 claims are blocked; the one computation from the paper's Eq. (2) is tested. The notebook checks what the files hold.

Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 gives an IMP reduction of 1.33% (reading a, 1 - f/1.5) or 1.20% (reading b, relative to f at 3e-7 S/m) for a 10-fold rise of membrane conductivity, outside 2 +- 0.2%, and 11.87% (a) or 11.75% (b) for a 100-fold rise, inside 12 +- 1.2%. Both readings give the same result. The qualitative part of the statement holds, as a 1000-fold rise is needed to reduce IMP by more than half (57.4%). In a grid of radii 5 to 15 um and membrane thicknesses 3 to 7 nm (a variant, not the criterion), no combination puts both values within tolerance under reading (a); R = 8 um with d = 3 nm gives 2.19% and 18.3%. The computation uses no recordings.
deviations: None in method; Eq. (2) and its constants are those of Methods 2.3, and both readings of the criterion were run.

findings.statement: The dandiset names this paper (IsPublishedIn) but holds none of its recordings. Its 292 files are FluoVolt strobe-imaging time courses at one 1-us pulse amplitude per cell, the protocol the paper attributes to its reference [20] (Semenov et al. 2025, Bioelectrochemistry 168, 109143). The paper's sets of 40 baseline and 60 pulse images at 900 ns with field escalation, and its Di-8-ANEPPS, 0.3-us, Gd3+, two-pulse and Fluo-4 Ca2+ recordings, are absent, so 33 of the 34 claims cannot be tested.

The laser delay of each frame is not recorded; the files give only a start time and a nominal 6 Hz. The data show that the 70 frames are successive delays across the pulse (the response rises and falls over a median 19 frames at half peak, at frames 16 to 34 in forward files and at the same frames counted from the end in backward files), so the backward files hold the time course in reverse order. A step of about 50 ns is consistent with this but not shown.

Pulses are given in volts across electrodes stated as 1.00 mm apart; no field strength is given. The paper uses electrodes 1.6 mm apart and field strengths from Sim4Life modelling, so its V/cm values cannot be assigned to these files. At the same 40 V the response differs between sessions (median peak index 25.9% on 2023-05-08, 11.9% on 2023-09-26).

Each subject has two files for each combination of recording order (forward, backward) and anode side, with nothing in the files to tell the two apart. Subject CHO-20230925-c1 has 4 files where the others have 8. Each file images a field of several cells (2 to 12 connected parts of the membrane mask; touching cells form one part), while the paper analyses one cell per experiment; no file says which cell, if any, the subject is.

File sub-CHO-20230926-c1_obj-bcvqko shows a different field of view from the other files of its subject (median correlation of mean images 0.079, against 0.995 for files of one subject) and a session start of 2024-12-16, fourteen months after that subject's other files. Its response is weak (peak index 1.3%).

The stated anode side does not fix the sign of the response. In 35 of 37 subjects the sign flips between the files stated as anode above and below, but 9 files differ in sign from the majority of the other files of their subject with the same stated anode side (groups with a tied majority are not counted), and across sessions files stated as anode above are brighter at the top of the cells (2023-05-08) or at the bottom (2023-09-25, 2023-09-26), and both in different subjects of 2023-10-10. The image orientation relative to the electrodes is not stated.
In 220 of 292 files frame 0 is less than 0.8 times as bright as the median frame (median ratio 0.59), which the description does not explain.

The archive summary gives the species as 'Cricetulus griseus - Cricetulus aureus' for a CHO cell line (the files give NCBITaxon_10029, C. griseus only), and every subject has an age of P1D. The image series description mentions sine wave exposures, which no file holds.

Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 gives a 1.33% IMP reduction for a 10-fold rise of membrane conductivity, where Results 3.5 states about 2%; the 100-fold value (11.87%) matches the stated 12%.
